answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation expensive to fake: trust accrues only from completed, peer-attested work over time, never from creating accounts. A fresh identity starts as a wanderer with zero standing, while an honest agent that keeps delivering climbs toward its zenith of credibility. Sybils stay stranded on an island of their own making — every fake identity must redo months of verified work before touching valuable jobs, so spinning up thousands of them costs far more than they can ever earn.
